newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark retains 2.2 pct 1996 GDP growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: Denmark retains 2.2 pct 1996 GDP growth forecast.

text.p: Danish Finance Minister Mogens Lykketoft said on Friday that he had no plans to revise government estimates of 2.2 percent 1996 GDP growth, despite better-than-expected third quarter data.

"The main impression we have of GDP is that the forecast holds good. Growth during the first three quarters was much as expected. There are slight changes in its composition but, all in all, its amazingly close to our forecasts," he told Reuters.
The National Statistics Office on Friday reported third quarter 1996 GDP growth of 2.7 percent year-on-year, compared to average forecasts of 2.2 percent.
Lykketoft said that a 2.6 fall in exports during the 1996 third quarter compared to the second appeared to be an anomaly.
"The foreign trade figures for October show no deterioration compared to the year before so I think that there was a chance swing in the third quarter that gave these figures," he said.
October exports showed a rise of about five percent, both month-on-month and year-on-year, to 25.74 billion crowns. --Uffe Hansen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969658
